correctness.rationale: Exact lumping to (number of vertices, visited count) gives discovery intensity lambda*(N-X)/(N-1). The exact imbalance R=(X-1)-alpha*(N-1) has negative drift -lambda*R/(N-1) and O(t) second moment; its compensated birth/discovery martingales have asymptotic brackets beta*t and a*t with zero cross-bracket. Their joint functional martingale CLT and a small-time cutoff for the k/s limiting linear drift yield the explicit Itô-integral Gaussian law. Exact rational finite-state reduction, generator, and covariance algebra checks passed 9369 assertions. The martingale proof, not the finite checker, establishes asymptotic correctness.

value.rationale: A primary 2021 probability paper specifically proposes random vertex generation times, but performs its Gaussian visit-count analysis with deterministic vertex generation. Independent Poisson birth times are a natural fluctuating-network model, and the explicit joint covariance identifies how demographic randomness propagates into discovery uncertainty, including a nonzero birth/discovery cross-covariance and a changed variance at unit rates. The theorem is a structural Gaussian fluctuation law across all positive birth and movement rates rather than an unmotivated finite numerical calculation.
